note: Declared differences between the solver as it is now and the Phase-0 baseline's recorded work counts. The baseline is the project's before-picture and is not re-recorded; a change that legitimately moves a checkpoint count is written down here instead, with the reason, so the tripwire in test/perf-harness.cjs keeps failing on a change nobody declared. Objectives are never declared here: a virtual run's objective must reproduce the baseline exactly, and any change to it is a quality regression rather than drift.

runs.reason: WS1.2's clock-sampling stride moves the probe at which the run observes its deadline, WS1.4 drops the seeds the margin stage has already optimised (seed-start 24 -> 20), and WS1.5 prices only the repair moves that could close a shortfall (repair-job 31416 -> 15446, freeing the budget the climb then spends: climb-job 82139 -> 98018). The run is deadline-bound, so the total is the budget either way; what moved is where it went. The objective is unchanged to the last bit.

Structural, and the largest declared drift in the file: Line switching now runs on a solve control. Phase-0 built one only in static mode, so this path was never checkpointed and the baseline records controls 0 and work.total 0 with an empty histogram — not a cheap run, an unmetered one, whose 50.4M units of LP cost sat outside any budget and outside the user's cancel. Charging it to a control makes that cost visible (work.total 0 -> 9454141, all of it dense) and bounding and deduplicating the phase LPs then cuts the work itself: lpMaximize 10 -> 4, pivots 2895 -> 681, tableau rows 176 -> 62, lp.work 50425171 -> 9454141. projectSchedule and projectPhase call counts are unchanged, so the schedule this measures is the same schedule. The objective is unchanged to the last bit.
